item.title: President Lee and Former President Moon Call for "Unity Within the Democratic Party"... Will the Convention Conflict Be Resolved? (이 대통령·문 전 대통령 “민주당 내 단합”…전대 갈등 수습될까)
item.description:
President Lee Jae-myung and former President Moon Jae-in jointly emphasized "unity" within the Democratic Party of Korea during a lunch meeting on the 1st, driven by a perceived need to mend the overheated and divisive atmosphere surrounding the August 17th party convention. With a structure emerging where the pro-Lee faction appears to support former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok and the pro-Moon faction seems to back former Representative Jeong Cheong-rae, attention is focused on whether this meeting between the current and former presidents will become a turning point for resolving the conflict. (이재명 대통령과 문재인 전 대통령이 1일 함께한 오찬에서 더불어민주당 내 ‘단합’을 한목소리로 강조한 것은, 8·17 민주당 전당대회가 과열돼 분열 양상을 띠는 것을 봉합할 필요성을 느꼈기 때문이다. 당내 친이재명(친명)계는 김민석 전 국무총리를, 친문재인(친문)계는 정청래 전 대표를 지지하는 듯한 구도가 형성된 가운데 두 전현직 대통령의 만남이 갈등 수습의 변곡점이 될지 주목된다.)

During his opening remarks at the lunch held at the presidential office, former President Moon stated, "President Lee is the only person in South Korea capable of achieving the Democratic Party's unity, greater unity with the democratic reform camp, and even national integration." He added, "I hope you will exercise greater leadership and surely realize the dream of becoming everyone's president." In response, President Lee said, "Internal unity is important, and we must constantly strive to expand our external reach to build structural majorities. We need to harmonize both aspects well." These remarks could be interpreted as former President Moon placing weight on "internal unity," while President Lee focused on "expanding external reach." <<> Regarding this, the presidential office explained that the two concepts are not separate. Chief Political Secretary Hong Ik-pyo, in a briefing at the Chungham Pavilion after the meeting, stated, "It means that only through unity can external expansion be possible, and only by expanding externally while uniting can a democratic government succeed." He added, "The two agreed that we must not act aggressively or insultingly toward each other." According to Democratic Party Rep. Yoon Geon-young, former President Moon, before heading back to his residence in Pyeongsan Village, Yangsan, South Gyeongsang Province, after the meeting, said, "It was a satisfactory meeting. We had a candid and open conversation about overall state affairs. Compared to when I came up to Seoul, I feel much more at ease now heading down to Pyeongsan." <<> The message from the current and former presidents is seen as expressing concern over the internal party conflict, which has escalated into an emotional fight ahead of the convention. <<> Recently, on online communities, Democratic Party supporters have been dividing themselves, creating derogatory terms that lump key figures from the pro-Lee and pro-Moon factions and exchanging mutual criticism. Additionally, the party leadership contenders and key figures have "entered" the debate over political legitimacy. After former Rep. Jeong Cheong-rae promoted himself as a "Roh Moo-hyun kid," Rep. Song Young-gil brought up claims that Rep. Jeong did not attend former President Roh's funeral and subsequently apologized. Author Yoo Si-min also appeared on Kim Eo-joon's YouTube channel on the 26th of last month and criticized President Lee's stance on external expansion, stating, "President Lee seems to be trying to do a reconstruction (not the expansion supporters wanted)." Following this, a series of polls indicated a decline in approval ratings for President Lee and the ruling party. It is against this backdrop that the current and former presidents, who had not had a meeting at the presidential office for over a year, met and emphasized "unity." <<> Major contenders for the Democratic Party leadership responded positively to the message from the current and former presidents. Former Prime Minister Kim wrote on his X account, "Even when fighting an opponent, dignity is needed, so much more so among comrades. Respect and restraint are internal traditions that have run through the eras of Kim Dae-jung, Roh Moo-hyun, Moon Jae-in, and Lee Jae-myung. They need to be restored." Former Rep. Jeong, meeting with reporters before the inauguration ceremony for Governor Lee Won-taek at the North Jeolla Provincial Office, said, "Within the Democratic Party, we must achieve grand unity, bringing supporters of former Presidents Kim Dae-jung, Roh Moo-hyun, and Moon Jae-in together. Further expanding our external reach is the path the Democratic Party must take to reclaim power." Rep. Song Young-gil also wrote on Facebook, "I believe that creating results through unity and expansion and proving them with those results to build a 'true ruling party' is the way to respond to the two former leaders' advice." <<> Rep. Kim Nam-jun said in a phone call with The Hankyoreh, "There is growing fatigue with the way people attack each other by bringing up the past, so it seems the two presidents sent a message against division." A first-term lawmaker commented, "We need to stop backward-looking negativity and compete on 'truly performing well' as the ruling party." However, many around the party predict it will not be easy to stop the competition for the party leadership, as the stakes involve nominations for the general election two years from now, and the race is already heating up. <<> Meanwhile, President Lee and former President Moon also exchanged views on issues such as prosecution reform and inter-Korean relations. <<> Chief Secretary Hong stated, "Regarding prosecution reform, which is a very important government reform task, they agreed that it is crucial for ensuring the democratization of our society and preventing the abuse of power by the prosecution in the future. Former President Moon said, 'While acting quickly is important, the government should push forward more carefully and meticulously to prevent harm or adverse effects on the people.'" Former President Moon advised on inter-Korean relations that "If we knock on the door for dialogue, opportunities will arise again." President Lee expressed frustration, saying, "I feel the inter-Korean relationship has been broken beyond repair. Yoon Seok-yeol's government's military pressure on the North for the sake of a self-coup was truly excessive." He added, "I will continue the policies for inter-Korean peaceful coexistence, starting from the Sunshine Policy that democratic governments have pursued." (문 전 대통령은 이날 청와대에서 열린 오찬 머리발언에서 “민주당의 단합, 민주개혁 진영과의 더 큰 단합, 그리고 국민 통합까지 나아갈 일을 해낼 수 있는 사람이 대한민국에서는 이 대통령뿐”이라며 “더 큰 리더십을 발휘하셔서 모두의 대통령이라는 꿈을 반드시 이루시길 바란다”고 말했다. 이에 이 대통령은 “내부 단합도 중요하고, 끊임없이 외연을 확장해 구조적 다수를 만들기 위해 노력해야 한다. 두가지를 잘 조화롭게 해야 한다”고 말했다. 문 전 대통령은 ‘내부 단합’에, 이 대통령은 ‘외연 확장’에 무게를 둔 듯한 뉘앙스로 풀이할 수도 있는 발언이었다.)

Reporter Seo Young-ji yj@hani.co.kr Reporter Kim Chae-woon cwk@hani.co.kr (이에 대해 청와대는 두가지가 별개가 아니라고 설명했다. 홍익표 청와대 정무수석은 회동 뒤 춘추관 브리핑에서 “단합을 해야 외연 확장이 가능하고, 외연 확장을 하면서 단합해야만 민주 정부가 성공할 수 있다는 뜻”이라며 “서로에게 공격적이거나 모욕적 방식으로 하면 안 된다는 데 두분이 뜻을 같이했다”고 덧붙였다. 문 대통령은 회동 뒤 사저가 있는 경남 양산시 평산마을로 향하기 전 “만족스러운 회동이었다. 국정 전반에 관해 허심탄회하게 이야기를 나눴다. 서울에 올라올 때보다 평산으로 내려가는 지금, 한결 마음이 놓인다”고 말했다고 윤건영 민주당 의원이 전했다.)

item.title: Palestinian Child Bana's Drawings, Who Hates School and Homework, Cross War and Division (학교와 숙제를 싫어하는 팔레스타인 어린이 ‘바나’의 그림, 전쟁과 분단을 넘다)
item.description:
"Coming to the Korean Peninsula, I feel a much stronger sense of kinship than when I went to other countries." <<> Tasameh Ramadan, director of the civic group 'Sij' which provides youth community education in Palestine, met with The Hankyoreh at the National Assembly on the 25th and cited war and division as commonalities between the situations facing South Korea and Palestine. Director Tasameh attended the exhibition of 'Drawing Hope', an international peace project where children from conflict zones like Palestine draw pictures, held that day at the National Assembly Members' Office Building by the North Korea aid organization 'Friends of Children'. <<> She said, "Just like separated families in Korea, it is common in Palestine for families to be separated by barriers and checkpoints." Israel occupies the West Bank and has erected separation barriers in many places, citing the need to 'protect Israeli citizens from terrorism'. <<> Director Tasameh calmly recounted the bleak reality of Palestinians who must check on their families' well-being through their fingertips. "There is a mother and daughter among my neighbors who live apart, separated by a wall. They try to find cracks or small holes in the wall to touch each other, even if just with their fingers," she said. It is said that Palestinians who have become separated families due to such barriers wander looking for holes in the wall, hoping for even a 'fingertip reunion'. She found this scene similar to the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) on the divided Korean Peninsula, the barbed wire, separated families, and the severance of free movement. While the causes and forms of war and division experienced by South Korea and Palestine differ, she said they are alike in that people cannot meet those they want to, and tension and hostility are a part of daily life. <<> Palestine Youth Community Education
Teaching Survival Skills Like First Aid
'Through Gunfire, Checkpoints, and Separation from Family,
Children Accumulate Layers of Isolation and Frustration' <<> War brutally cuts away even the childhood memories of Palestinian people. As children grow up, they experience Israeli checkpoints, gunfire, and separation from family. Director Tasameh said, "Palestinians must have the ability to remain calm and provide first aid to a wounded friend if they are walking down the road and suddenly Israeli soldiers open fire." So 'Sij' also teaches youth emergency training like first aid and responding to explosives. In a Palestinian reality where no one knows when gunfire will start or when infrastructure will collapse, such preparation has become a survival skill. <<> Director Tasameh described the hardest aspect for Palestinian children as "a life robbed of childhood." She said that when she first went abroad at age 14, she was shocked that there were no checkpoints when moving between cities. "In Palestine, I thought it was natural that you had to pass through a checkpoint to go anywhere," she said. As time passes, the wounds, frustration, and isolation of Palestinian children accumulate in layers, but the urgency of surviving in Palestine means that caring for these children's trauma and healing their minds is always pushed aside. <<> Director Tasameh explained that the very process of Palestinian children participating in the 'Drawing Hope' project—drawing pictures on the theme of 'hope' and expressing their suppressed emotions while receiving empathy—was the beginning of healing. What was particularly impressive was the way solidarity was created through the drawings. The children asked questions like "Do Korean people know about us?" and "Are we not alone?", and they felt great significance in being connected to the world through their drawings. She said, "While protest rallies supporting Palestine are also important, children's drawings appeal to the heart more directly." <<> Hosted by North Korea Aid Group Friends of Children
Participating in an Exhibition of Conflict Zone Children's Drawings
'Connection to the World Through Drawings Holds Great Meaning' <<> Kim Dong-jin, director of Friends of Children, who interpreted the interview that day, said, "Drawing Hope continuously asks us, 'In an era where war and division have become routine, how can people live together in harmony?' When we empathize with the pain of people in other regions and encounter our shared humanity through the eyes of children, we gain new imagination and hope regarding our own social reality." <<> In the frank greeting from 11-year-old Palestinian child Bana, whose drawing was displayed in 'Drawing Hope'—"I really hate school and homework"—adults are confronted with how threadbare the garment of division they wear truly is. <<> Lee Ki-bum, chairman of Friends of Children, emphasized the significance of the event, where children send messages to friends in societies with different histories of conflict through their drawings, saying, "Children are trying to overcome the walls of war and conflict that adults have created, through drawings of peace." After the exhibition at the National Assembly, the children's drawings will be displayed at Imjingak, Gyeonggi Province, until the 31st of this month. <<> The Drawing Hope exhibition originated from Friends of Children's inter-Korean children's drawing exchange project. Since 1996, Friends of Children has been facilitating activities where North and South Korean children, unable to meet due to division, draw and exchange self-portraits. These activities expanded to East Asia, including Japan and China, and developed into the 'East Asian Children's Peace Drawing Exhibition' starting in 2001. Later, through solidarity from around the world that resonated with messages of courage and peace, it expanded in 2023 into Drawing Hope, with children from various countries participating. Exhibitions have been held in Los Angeles, USA (2023), Belfast, Northern Ireland (2024), and Cape Town, South Africa (last year). <<> For the past 30 years, Friends of Children has strived to create a Korean Peninsula where children from North and South can play together, arm-in-arm. To walk arm-in-arm, one needs similar height and mutual understanding. Friends of Children conducts peace education so that children in the South can grow up peacefully, and provides humanitarian aid and inter-Korean cooperation activities so that children in the North can grow up healthy and walk arm-in-arm at the same height. <<> Director Tasameh asked young South Koreans to "move beyond accepting division as a natural reality and recognize the structure that creates it." She concluded the interview by saying to young South Koreans, "Come visit Palestine." It was a wish for a peaceful era to come soon, where young South Koreans can travel to Palestine. <<> Text and photos by reporter Kwon Hyuk-chul nura@hani.co.kr (“다른 나라를 갔을 때보다 한반도에 오니 훨씬 동질감을 많이 느낍니다.”)
